organizations.name: Taliban

events.description: UN Monitoring Team submitted its 1988 report on the Taliban and other groups in Afghanistan (released mid-December 2025), a 17-month gap since the previous report; states Taliban claims of no foreign terrorists are 'not credible' and >20 groups remain active.
actors: UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team

events.description: UNSC renewed the Monitoring Team's 1988 mandate for 14 months, moving expiry to February 2026; renewal not a foregone conclusion.
actors: UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team

events.description: US killed Ayman al-Zawahiri in Kabul; Taliban continue to deny he was ever in Afghanistan.
Islamic State attacks in Kerman, Iran and at Crocus City Hall, Moscow (early 2024), facilitated at least by ISKP per the UN report.
Afghanistan-Pakistan border hostilities escalated almost to war over TTP attacks launched from Afghan soil; Turkey brokered an uneasy truce.
Sirajuddin Haqqani left Afghanistan for a few months after asserting independence on women's education, then returned pledging unity and allegiance to Hibatullah.
Former deputy foreign minister Stanikzai effectively exiled after publicly opposing the girls' education ban.
International Criminal Court indicted Hibatullah Akhundzada and chief justice Abdul Hakim Haqqani for gender persecution / crimes against humanity against women.
US raid on al-Qaeda camps in Shorabak, Kandahar killed ~200 fighters; US estimate revised from 50-100 to 200-300.
Mullah Omar died; Taliban concealed his death for two years and issued statements in his name; disclosure in 2015 drove some factions to the Islamic State.
7 October 2023 Hamas attack; since then the Gaza narrative has narrowed the gap between al-Qaeda and Iran's axis of resistance.
Syrian President al-Sharaa played basketball with CENTCOM commander Admiral Cooper (hosts cite sarcastically).
UN Monitoring Team began direct conversations with the Taliban ('just over a year ago') and members now travel to Afghanistan.

key_claims: The Taliban's claim that no foreign terrorist groups are in Afghanistan is 'not credible' (UN); >20 groups remain, led by TTP (~6,000), ISKP (~2,000), al-Qaeda/AQIS (200-300, hosts say too low), TIP, Jamaat Ansarullah and Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan.
The Taliban actively host TTP and AQIS, which have blended together and use Afghan soil to attack Pakistan, nearly causing war in 2025 — the scorpion stinging the frog once across the river.

Al-Qaeda's infrastructure (camps in 12 of 34 provinces, madrasas, media centre, depot, senior commanders in Kabul) is unchanged; member states may be withholding al-Qaeda information to avoid the optics of the withdrawal and to preserve the Taliban-as-CT-partner narrative.
Saif al-Adel is in Iran, not Afghanistan, and has partially integrated al-Qaeda into Iran's axis of resistance; the UN report's wording risks implying he is in Afghanistan.

Partnering with the Taliban or al-Sharaa against ISIS is strategically wrong and ethically unjustifiable: 'you can't trust terrorists to fight terrorists, and you can't trust terrorists to vet terrorists'.

Hibatullah has consolidated unquestionable authority from Kandahar; Haqqani and Stanikzai were corralled or exiled for dissent; Kabul 'political actors' will try to outlive Hibatullah rather than challenge him; Yaqoob (Omar's son) is the likeliest successor, with a Haqqani-Yaqoob axis.

The 'peace of the Taliban' is real only because the insurgents now run the state; women, girls and minorities lose out; ICC indictments of Hibatullah and the chief justice are a rare accountability step.
Poppy cultivation is reportedly down 95% but methamphetamine/ephedra is the rising revenue stream and under-covered in the report; the Taliban retain their drug networks.
